text: Build, query, update; lazy tags for range add.

A segment tree (线段树) splits [1, n] into halves again and again; every node stores a summary (sum, max, …) of its range. Node p has children 2p and 2p + 1, like a heap. Any range [l, r] is covered by O(log n) nodes (green: [1, 4] = [1, 3] + [4, 4]), so queries and updates cost O(log n).
Unlike prefix sums and Fenwick trees, a segment tree can store anything that two halves can be combined into: sums, max/min, max subarray, counts of colours. Allocate 4n nodes.

Lazy propagation (懒标记): adding v to a whole range would touch every leaf. Instead, when a node's range lies fully inside the update, update its sum (+ v × length) and leave a note "add v to my children later" in tag[p] . Push the note down only when a later operation needs to go below that node.

text: Every update and query follows the same three cases: node range outside [x, y] → ignore; fully inside → use or mark this node; otherwise → push down, recurse into both halves, push up.
Push down before going into the children, in both update and query, or children answer with stale values. Sums reach 10¹⁸: use long long for sums and tags.

This is the template for range add + range sum (P3372). Range max/min only changes pushup (max instead of +) and what a tag does to a node (P1816). Flipping lights on a range keeps the count of lit lights and a "flip" tag that toggles (P3870).
Two tags in order; nodes that keep several numbers.

Two kinds of tags at once need an order. For "multiply then add", store each node's pending change as x → x · mul + add. A new multiply c turns it into x · (mul·c) + add·c; a new add c turns it into x · mul + (add + c). Push both down together.

Writing every pending change as the same shape (x · mul + add) makes combining two changes a small formula, so any order of operations is handled by one apply (P3373). "Set to v" plus "add v" (P1253) works the same way with an "assigned?" flag that clears the add.

title: Merging more than one number per node

text: The best subarray of a range lies in the left half, in the right half, or crosses the middle (进阶篇第3章). Each node keeps four numbers so that two halves can always be merged: total, best prefix, best suffix, best inside. Queries merge the O(log n) nodes they meet (P4513).

Variance (P1471) keeps Σx and Σx²; the longest alternating run (P6492) keeps run lengths at both ends; square roots on ranges (P4145) stop once a node's max is 1. Design the node first: "what must I know about each half to answer for the whole?"
A tree over values: counts and the k-th smallest.

A value segment tree (权值线段树) is built over values instead of positions: leaf v counts how many times v has appeared. It answers "how many seen values are ≤ x" and "what is the k-th smallest seen value" in O(log V); discretise first if values are large.

k-th smallest: walk down from the root; if the left child holds at least k values go left, otherwise subtract its count and go right. Counting increasing triples (P1637): fix the middle element; multiply "smaller values before it" by "larger values after it", both counts over values, so a value tree or the equivalent Fenwick tree (进阶篇第5章) does the job. Inversions (P1908) and point sets with "first point to the upper right" (CF19D) also count over values.
A value tree needs a leaf for every possible value. Values up to 10⁹ must be discretised (第2章) first, or the tree built dynamically, creating nodes only when they are reached.
The Luogu problems for this chapter, a ladder through them, and experiments to try yourself.
Key points to memorise
1. Node p covers [l, r]; children 2p, 2p + 1 split at m = (l + r) / 2; 4n nodes.
2. Three cases: outside → ignore; inside → use / tag; else → pushdown, recurse, pushup.
3. Lazy add: sum += v·len, tag += v; push down before visiting children.
4. Two tags: store x → x·mul + add; new mul c: (mul·c, add·c); new add c: (mul, add + c).
5. Design nodes by "what must I know about each half to answer for the whole?"
6. Max subarray node: sum, best prefix, best suffix, best inside.
7. Value tree: leaf v counts v; k-th smallest walks left if cnt[left] ≥ k.
8. Large values: discretise first (or build nodes on demand).
